what: SBA Communications owns and leases mobile phone towers. Operators rent space on its structures to hang antennas, under long leases with annual price increases built in. It operates in the United States, Latin America and Africa.
customers: Mobile network operators in the United States, Brazil, other Latin American countries, South Africa and Tanzania.
money: US tower leases to mobile operators
towers in Latin America and Africa
moat: Tower sites with planning permission and existing tenants, where adding a second or third operator to the same structure costs almost nothing and is nearly all profit.
risks: Debt of about $13 billion against little cash
Mobile operator consolidation reduces the number of potential tenants per tower
Brazilian and African currency movements affect international revenue
US carrier capital spending has been restrained
opportunities: Operating margin of 48% and net margin of 37%
Analysts see about 32% upside from current levels
Leases include contractual annual price increases regardless of new tenants
watch: Organic tower leasing revenue growth and tenant additions per tower.
